lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Coffee Roasters | Barista | Metro City, USA | Oct 2025 - Present
- Prepared drinks for the morning rush of about 200 orders and kept the bar stocked.
- Opened the café three days a week and handled the daily cash count.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Migrated 40 department sites to a shared component library, cutting new-page build time from 2 days to half a day.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; my findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Writes the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybook, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Education appears before Experience and Projects.
items.because: The résumé does not lead with the most relevant development work.

items.says: The morning-rush duties and order count describe work and workload, not an outcome.
“cafØ” is a corrupted spelling.
items.because: The corrupted character makes a common word look like a typo and can distract a reader.

items.says: The opening and cash-counting duties have no stated outcome.
“Handled the daily cash count” uses a vague verb.
The Barista entry lists routine duties but gives little context for a software-development direction.
items.because: The details do not connect to the development experience elsewhere and take space from more relevant work.

items.says: “Page performance by 35%” does not identify the metric or its comparison.
items.because: Without a baseline and defined metric, the scale of the improvement is hard to interpret.

items.says: The repeated “by” makes the gain and implementation sound clumsy.
“Flagged in the audit” is redundant after “accessibility issues.”
“Which caught” makes the connection between the tests and regressions less direct.
“By adding” could be tightened without losing the implementation detail.
Storing user input in React state does not prevent XSS when it is rendered with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
items.because: React state does not sanitize HTML, and `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` bypasses React’s normal escaping.

items.says: The XSS-prevention claim has no verification result or evidence.
items.because: Without a security test or audit result, the claim is difficult to assess.

items.says: The result is buried after the technology and implementation details.
items.because: A scanning reader encounters the method before the load-time and booking gains.

items.says: “My findings” uses a first-person pronoun in a résumé bullet.
“Writes” is the wrong tense.
“Search time” does not specify what the 4 seconds to under 1 measures.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether it means page time, query response time, or time to find a course.

items.says: “Showing live bus arrivals” does not explain how the app retrieves or updates arrival information.
The faster load-time result appears after the implementation detail.
“And” does not clarify the relationship between open-sourcing the app and the agency linking it.
The project heading says Vue, but the bullet says the booking flow used React and TypeScript.
items.because: The framework mismatch makes the technology description less credible unless different parts used different frameworks.

items.says: “Worked on the frontend” is vague and does not name the specific action performed.
The booking-flow contribution has no stated result.
The calendar component and its tests are described without a result.
The calendar-component result is not the opening point of the project entry.
The travel-search bullet does not clearly belong with the library room-booking project.
items.because: The other bullets describe library booking, while this one resembles work in the Lumen Travel internship.

items.says: The booking increase does not specify the booking measure or its comparison.
items.because: Without that context, “about a tenth” is difficult to interpret.

items.says: The travel-search achievement closely matches the Lumen Travel internship achievement and may look duplicated.
items.because: Both describe a travel-search rebuild with server rendering and a booking gain, casting doubt on whether they are separate achievements.
